title: RS256 algorithm with string secret causes runtime InvalidKeyError
description: `auth.py` sets `ALGORITHM = SecurityConfig.JWT_ALGORITHM` which defaults to `"RS256"` via env, then calls `jwt.encode(to_encode, SECRET_KEY, algorithm=ALGORITHM)` where `SECRET_KEY` is a plain string from `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`. The `python-jose` library raises `InvalidKeyError: Could not deserialize key data` when RS256 is used with a string key — RSA requires actual RSA key objects. Every POST /api/v1/auth/token and /register will fail unless `JWT_ALGORITHM=HS256` is set in env.
recommendation: Switch `auth.py` to use `get_jwt_manager()` (already imported at line 15) for token creation/validation, or add env guard: if ALGORITHM != "HS256", load RSA key from env/secrets-manager rather than using JWT_SECRET_KEY string.
acceptance_test_hint: `POST /api/v1/auth/token` with valid credentials returns 200 (not 500); `pytest tests/test_auth.py::test_login` passes

title: REST trigger endpoints unauthenticated — any caller can broadcast messages
description: `POST /api/v1/ws/trigger/alert` and `POST /api/v1/ws/trigger/news` have no authentication `Depends`. Any unauthenticated HTTP client can send arbitrary alert messages to specific connected users or broadcast news headlines to all WebSocket clients. The alert endpoint also accepts free-form `alert_type` and `message` parameters with no validation.
recommendation: Add `current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)` (or `get_current_admin_user`) to both endpoints. Add input validation (enum for alert_type, length cap on message).
acceptance_test_hint: Unauthenticated `POST /api/v1/ws/trigger/alert` returns 401; authenticated admin call succeeds

title: GET /ws/connections exposes client IDs and subscriptions — no auth
description: `GET /api/v1/ws/connections` returns `total_connections`, full list of `client_id` strings, per-client symbol subscriptions, and active stream symbols. No authentication or authorization is required. This leaks user activity patterns and client identifiers.
recommendation: Add `current_user = Depends(get_current_admin_user)` dependency. Consider returning aggregated counts only for non-admin roles.
acceptance_test_hint: Unauthenticated GET returns 401; admin-authenticated call returns 200 with connection data

title: market and portfolio WebSocket endpoints have no authentication
description: `market_data_stream_endpoint` (line 170) and `portfolio_stream` (line 186) accept WebSocket connections with `await websocket.accept()` and no `@secure_websocket` decorator, no JWT check, no rate limiting. The portfolio stream broadcasts portfolio-specific updates using the raw `portfolio_id` path parameter with no ownership check.
recommendation: Apply `@secure_websocket(require_auth=True)` to both endpoints, or at minimum add a token query parameter validated against `WebSocketSecurityManager`. Add ownership check in portfolio_stream to verify the authenticated user owns portfolio_id.
acceptance_test_hint: Anonymous WebSocket connection to `/api/v1/ws/market` is rejected (4008 policy violation); authenticated user cannot access another user's portfolio stream

title: jwt_manager imported but unused in auth router
description: `from backend.security.jwt_manager import get_jwt_manager, TokenClaims` is imported at line 15, but neither `get_jwt_manager` nor `TokenClaims` is used anywhere in auth.py. The router implements its own `create_access_token()` / `get_current_user()` functions with plain `jwt.encode/decode`. This means the advanced jwt_manager (RSA keys, Redis token blacklisting, refresh token rotation) is bypassed entirely for all auth flows in this router.
recommendation: Replace the bespoke `create_access_token`/`get_current_user` with `get_jwt_manager().create_token()` and `get_jwt_manager().verify_token()`. Remove the dead import.
acceptance_test_hint: `POST /api/v1/auth/token` returns a token verifiable by jwt_manager; blacklisted tokens are rejected

title: get_current_user defined in auth.py shadowed by auth.oauth2.get_current_user — duplicate implementations
description: `auth.py` defines its own `async def get_current_user(token, db)` at line 70 using `jwt.decode(token, SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[ALGORITHM])`. `backend/auth/oauth2.py` also exports `get_current_user` (imported by stocks.py, portfolio.py, trading.py etc). Two separate implementations with potentially different decoding keys and algorithms will produce different validation results for the same token.
recommendation: Delete the local `get_current_user` in auth.py and use `from backend.auth.oauth2 import get_current_user` consistently across all routers. Consolidate JWT decode logic in one place.
acceptance_test_hint: All routers import `get_current_user` from the same module; `backend/auth/oauth2.py` is the sole JWT validation point

title: No integration test for authentication failure path in /ws/stream
description: The `@secure_websocket` decorator enforces JWT auth on the main stream endpoint. There are no visible tests for the anonymous-connection rejection path, the rate-limit enforcement, or the subscription permission denial. Prior report listed 18 WS tests but the concurrent-connection and memory-leak gaps remain.
recommendation: Add pytest-asyncio tests: (1) anonymous connection to /ws/stream is rejected, (2) rate limit blocks >60 messages/min, (3) VIEWER role denied >10 symbol subscriptions.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/test_websocket*.py -k "test_anon_rejected or test_rate_limit or test_viewer_limit"` passes

title: create_access_token helper duplicates jwt_manager token logic — should be consolidated
description: `create_access_token()` in auth.py is a local function duplicating what `jwt_manager.create_token()` provides (with additional security: RSA keys, Redis blacklist, token versioning). Keeping both paths means security improvements to jwt_manager do not automatically apply to auth token creation.
recommendation: This is a corollary of F-01-009; fix F-01-009 first.
acceptance_test_hint: `create_access_token` in auth.py removed; all token creation flows through jwt_manager

title: Socket.IO server with `cors_allowed_origins="*"`
description: `sio = socketio.AsyncServer(async_mode="asgi", cors_allowed_origins="*", ...)`. Wildcard CORS on a real-time channel that emits authenticated portfolio data (`emit_portfolio_update`, `emit_alert_notification`). Combined with the absence of any auth check on subscription handlers (`subscribe_portfolio` accepts any `portfolio_id` from any client), this allows cross-origin pages to subscribe to arbitrary portfolios and alert streams once a user has a session cookie.
recommendation: Read `settings.CORS_ORIGINS` and pass to `cors_allowed_origins=settings.CORS_ORIGINS or []`. Add JWT verification to `connect()` handler via `auth` dict (Socket.IO supports per-handshake auth). Validate that `portfolio_id` belongs to the authenticated user before `enter_room`.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: connecting from a foreign origin without auth is rejected; subscribing to another user's portfolio returns `error` event.

title: Unauthenticated model management endpoints
description: `POST /models/{name}/load`, `DELETE /models/{name}`, and `POST /retrain` have no authentication. Server binds `0.0.0.0` with `allow_origins=["*"]`. Any network peer can unload production models or trigger compute-intensive retraining.
recommendation: Add API key or JWT auth to all mutating endpoints using FastAPI `Depends`. Restrict CORS origins to known frontend domains. Consider binding to `127.0.0.1` or behind an internal reverse proxy.
acceptance_test_hint: `curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8001/models/lstm_price_predictor` should return 401 without auth header

title: No integration tests for the ML API server endpoints
description: Test files `test_ml_pipeline.py` and `test_ml_performance.py` use mocks and unit-level tests. No tests exercise the live FastAPI `ml_api_server.py` via `TestClient`. Security-sensitive endpoints (`/retrain`, `/models/{name}/load`, `DELETE`) have zero test coverage.
recommendation: Add `TestClient(app)` integration tests for all CRUD endpoints in `ml_api_server.py`, including negative cases for path traversal and unauthenticated access.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/test_ml_api_server.py` passes with ≥80% endpoint coverage

title: MD5 used for cache key generation
description: `_generate_cache_key()` at line 764 uses `hashlib.md5()`. MD5 has known collision vulnerabilities. While not a security-critical use here (cache key only, no authentication), better_pattern is to use `hashlib.sha256()` or `hashlib.blake2b()` for consistency with any future security-sensitive hash usage.
recommendation: Replace `hashlib.md5` with `hashlib.sha256` in cache key generation.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep "hashlib.md5" backend/ml/feature_store.py` returns no results

title: Ephemeral fallback for SESSION/JWT_SECRET_KEY
description: `os.getenv(..., secrets.token_urlsafe(32))` — env unset → random per process; multi-worker gives N distinct keys
recommendation: Raise RuntimeError at import time when production env unset; remove token_urlsafe default from class-level expression
acceptance_test_hint: Test that missing env in production raises

title: Naive/aware datetime breaks revoke_token
description: `datetime.fromtimestamp(exp)` naive vs `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` aware → TypeError on every revoke; swallowed by bare except
recommendation: `datetime.fromtimestamp(exp, tz=timezone.utc)`; add unit test; replace bare except
acceptance_test_hint: pytest test_revoke_blacklists_token passes

title: HS256 fallback path with ephemeral secret
description: RS256→HS256 algorithm-confusion fallback when JWT manager init fails; combined with F-08-002, fallback tokens unverifiable across worker restarts
recommendation: Remove HS256 fallback; propagate init errors as 500
acceptance_test_hint: grep returns 0 outside config + tests

title: Redis fallback returns None, blacklist silently degrades
description: Redis outage allows revoked tokens to be re-used (`_is_token_blacklisted` returns False when client is None)
recommendation: Circuit-breaker; fail-secure on degraded state; Prometheus alert
acceptance_test_hint: Chaos test: stop Redis mid-traffic, assert 503s

title: CSRF exempts /login and /register
description: Combined with allow_credentials=True, increases credential-stuffing surface
recommendation: Tighten origin/referer validation for those endpoints; tighten CORS for login
acceptance_test_hint: curl POST with malicious Origin returns 403

title: MFA secrets stored under predictable username key
description: Allows enumeration; collision on username reuse
recommendation: Use stable user_id (UUID)
acceptance_test_hint: New users get unique IDs after username reuse

title: jwt.decode without signature verification before revoke
description: Trusts client claims; attacker forges huge `exp` to flood blacklist Redis
recommendation: Cap derived TTL at access-token max regardless of claim
acceptance_test_hint: Forged exp=2099 token blacklisted with TTL ≤ access_token_expire

title: Two competing exception hierarchies
description: `backend/exceptions.py` defines `ValidationError`, `AuthenticationError`, `NotFoundError`, etc. (suffix `Error`, base `AppException`). `backend/utils/exceptions.py` defines `ValidationException`, `AuthenticationException`, `NotFoundException`, etc. (suffix `Exception`, base `InvestmentAnalysisException`). Repositories import the former; rate limiter & kafka_client import the latter. No common base.
recommendation: Pick one canonical module (recommend `backend/exceptions.py` — shorter, used by repos and services). Migrate `RateLimitException`, `DataIngestionException`, `ExternalAPIException`, etc. into it. Re-export legacy names with deprecation warnings during transition.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/ -k 'exception or validation'` passes; `grep -rn "from backend.utils.exceptions"` returns only the shim.

title: `_user_to_dict` uses `getattr` for 10 fields
description: Suggests fragile coupling between User ORM and dict consumers. Each call walks 10 attributes.
recommendation: Replace with a Pydantic `UserPublic` model (`from_attributes=True`); reuse across routers.
acceptance_test_hint: `backend/utils/auth.py::get_current_user` returns `UserPublic`-derived dict; routers updated; tests pass.

title: Login thunk stores `response.data.token` but refresh interceptor stores `response.data.access_token`
description: Login path: `appSlice.ts:68` sets `localStorage.setItem('access_token', response.data.token)`. Refresh path in `api.service.ts:57-58`: `const { access_token } = response.data; localStorage.setItem('access_token', access_token)`. Even if fixed for the backend response structure, these two code paths use different destructuring patterns and must remain in sync.
recommendation: Centralise token persistence in a `tokenStorage.ts` utility (`setAccessToken`, `getAccessToken`, `clearTokens`) used by both `appSlice.ts` and `api.service.ts`. This eliminates the sync problem.
acceptance_test_hint: Unit tests for `tokenStorage` module; both login and refresh paths call the same setter

title: Login thunk `access_token` extraction not unit-tested
description: `slices.test.ts` tests `login.fulfilled` (line 219) but does not verify `localStorage.setItem` was called with the correct token value. The F-12-002 bug would not be caught by the existing test.
recommendation: Add assertion: `expect(localStorageMock.setItem).toHaveBeenCalledWith('access_token', 'expected-token')` in the login thunk test.
acceptance_test_hint: Login test fails before fix and passes after fix

title: JWT manager fixture uses MagicMock — no test covers actual JWTManager.create_token with RS256 key
description: `TestJWTManagerTokenCreation.jwt_manager_mock` (line 72–91) creates a `MagicMock()` object, not a real `JWTManager`. No test in `backend/tests/security/` or `backend/tests/test_security_compliance.py` exercises the production `JWTManager` with the RSA key pair from `security_config.py`. Scope 08 (F-08-001) found hardcoded salt in `secrets_manager.py` that undermines all stored JWT keys; scope 01 (F-01-001) found the RS256/HS256 algorithm confusion. Neither risk is covered by a test that instantiates the real class.
recommendation: Add integration-level test that calls `get_jwt_manager()` (the production factory) and verifies `create_token` + `validate_token` roundtrip succeeds with RS256 and fails gracefully when algorithm is wrong.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/security/test_security_modules.py -k "jwt" -v` exercises real JWTManager

title: TestAuthenticationSecurity.jwt_manager fixture instantiates JWTManager with plain string secret
description: `JWTManager(secret_key="test_secret_key_12345678901234567890")` at line 74 creates a manager with an HS256-style string key. The production `JWTManager` uses RS256 with RSA key objects (confirmed by conftest.py:332 which uses `jwt_mgr.private_key`). The test therefore validates a different algorithm than production, meaning HS256-specific token behaviors (e.g., padding issues, algorithm confusion attacks) are tested against a configuration that doesn't match deployment.
recommendation: Update test fixture to use `get_jwt_manager()` from `backend.security.jwt_manager` or generate a test RSA key pair (as `backend/tests/security/test_security_modules.py:59-70` already does for `rsa_keys` fixture).
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/test_security_compliance.py::TestAuthenticationSecurity -v` passes with RS256-based fixture
